Discourse's Enum implementation (lib/enumerable_enum / enum used for Post.types, seen in the same diff as `Post.types = Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`) is 1-based: the first symbol gets value 1, matching the DB default for the existing `posts.type` column, which has always stored 1 for :regular. The migration's `default: 1` is therefore intentionally aligned with :regular = 1, so :raw_html = 2 and the backfill/new-post default is correct; the described site-wide 'raw markdown' breakage does not occur. Additionally, the new spec explicitly asserts `post.cook_method.should == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` for imported posts while regular posts use the default, which only works coherently with the 1-based Enum the code was written against.

judged_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 backfills every existing post with the value 1, but Post.cook_methods = Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) assigns sequential values starting at 0, so the default 1 maps to :raw_html instead of :regular. Every pre-existing post is reclassified as raw_html and every newly created regular post inherits the same column default (PostCreator only assigns cook_method when the option is passed, so all normal posts get the default), so Post#cook returns raw markdown site-wide: any edit or recook persists uncooked markdown into the cooked column and the rendering pipeline (markdown, emoji, oneboxes) silently disappears for all content.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on an assumption not shown in the diff: that `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` assigns values starting at 0. The diff provides no definition of `Enum`, and the migration explicitly sets `cook_method` default to `1`, which is consistent with an Enum implementation that starts at 1 (common in this codebase, e.g. `Post.types = Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)` elsewhere). If the Enum starts at 1, then default `1` correctly maps to `:regular` and does not reclassify all posts as `:raw_html`. Therefore the alleged site-wide breakage cannot be verified from this diff.
